source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּאַסְפ֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו כָּל־זִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king, and they gathered to him all [the] elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

en.L: And the king sent, and they gathered to him all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
en.B: Then the king sent word, and all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem were gathered to him.
en.R: Then King Josiah sent for all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem, and they came together to meet with him.

decisions.choice: the king: Josiah, acting on the word Huldah gave him
decisions.reason: The chapter goes straight on from chapter 22. The book found in the temple had been read to Josiah, and the prophet Huldah had said that the disaster it threatened would come, but not in his days, because he had humbled himself (22:8-20). His first act is to call the leaders of the nation together.

decisions.choice: the elders: the heads of families and towns
decisions.reason: The elders were the senior men who led the clans and towns and spoke for the people (1 Kings 8:1; 20:7). The king calls them before he calls the whole nation (verse 2).

decisions.choice: they gathered to him: the elders came at his summons
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only that the king "sent" and that "they gathered". He sent messengers, and the elders were brought together before him.

decisions.choice: King Josiah sent for ... they came together to meet with him
decisions.reason: Readable names the king and says what "sent" means here: he summoned the elders.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַל הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ בֵּית־יְהוָ֡ה וְכָל־אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָה֩ וְכָל־יֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם אִתּ֗וֹ וְהַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְהַנְּבִיאִ֔ים וְכָל־הָעָ֖ם לְמִקָּטֹ֣ן וְעַד־גָּד֑וֹל וַיִּקְרָ֣א בְאָזְנֵיהֶ֗ם אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵי֙ סֵ֣פֶר הַבְּרִ֔ית הַנִּמְצָ֖א בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up the king [to the] house of Yahweh, and every man of Judah and all [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets and all the people, from small and to great; and he read in their ears all [the] words of [the] book of the covenant which was found in [the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And the king went up [to the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and every man of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets and all the people, from small to great; and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The king went up to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and with him went {{gender:all the people of Judah|all the men of Judah}} and all who lived in Jerusalem, the priests and the prophets, and all the people, from the least to the greatest. In their hearing he read out all the words of the book of the covenant, which had been found in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The king went up to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. {{gender:All the people of Judah|All the men of Judah}} and everyone who lived in Jerusalem went with him. The priests and the prophets went too, and all the people, from the least important to the most important. The king read aloud to them everything written in the book of the covenant that had been found in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

decisions.choice: the book of the covenant: the scroll found in the temple
decisions.reason: This is the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the temple, called "the book of the law" in 22:8. It is named here for what it contains: the terms of Yahweh's covenant with Israel, with the curses that fall on those who break it (22:13, 16-17). What Josiah does in this chapter follows the commands of Deuteronomy closely: one place of worship (Deuteronomy 12), no high places, mediums or child sacrifice (Deuteronomy 18:9-12), and the Passover kept at the place Yahweh chooses (Deuteronomy 16:1-8).

decisions.choice: reading the covenant to the people: as Moses did at Sinai
decisions.reason: At Sinai Moses "took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people", and they promised to obey (Exodus 24:7). Deuteronomy 31:10-13 commands the law to be read before all Israel. Josiah does the same, and the people bind themselves to the covenant in verse 3.

decisions.choice: from small to great: everyone, whatever their rank or age
decisions.reason: The pair names the whole range of people, from the least important to the most important (1 Samuel 5:9; Jeremiah 6:13).

decisions.choice: every man of Judah: the people of Judah as a whole
decisions.reason: "Man of Judah" is used for the people of Judah taken together. The verse goes on to say that "all the people" were there.

decisions.choice: the prophets: the account in Chronicles has "the Levites"
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 34:30 tells the same event and names "the priests and the Levites". The text of Kings here has "the priests and the prophets", which is followed.

decisions.choice: all the people of Judah
decisions.reason: The phrase means the people of Judah as a whole (m4), so Balanced and Readable use the inclusive wording, with the traditional form as the alternative. Literal keeps "every man of Judah".

decisions.choice: temple of the LORD
decisions.reason: As throughout these books, Literal and Balanced say "house of the LORD", and Readable says "temple".

source.text: וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ עַֽל־הָ֨עַמּ֜וּד וַיִּכְרֹ֥ת אֶֽת־הַבְּרִ֣ית׀לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה לָלֶ֜כֶת אַחַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ וְלִשְׁמֹ֨ר מִצְוֺתָ֜יו וְאֶת־עֵדְוֺתָ֤יו וְאֶת־חֻקֹּתָיו֙ בְּכָל־לֵ֣ב וּבְכָל־נֶ֔פֶשׁ לְהָקִ֗ים אֶת־דִּבְרֵי֙ הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את הַכְּתֻבִ֖ים עַל־הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד כָּל־הָעָ֖ם בַּבְּרִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And stood the king by the pillar and cut the covenant before Yahweh, to walk after Yahweh and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all [the] heart and with all [the] soul, to establish [the] words of the covenant the this, the written on the book the this; and stood all the people in the covenant.

en.L: And the king stood by the pillar and made the covenant before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to walk after {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} testimonies and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes with all [the] heart and with all [the] soul, to carry out the words of this covenant that were written in this book; and all the people stood in the covenant.
en.B: The king stood by the pillar and made the covenant in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: to follow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decrees and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes with all his heart and all his being, and so to carry out the words of this covenant written in this book. And all the people committed themselves to the covenant.
en.R: The king stood by the pillar and made a covenant in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s presence. He promised to follow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instructions and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws with all his heart and all his life. He promised to do everything this covenant said, as it was written in this book. And all the people promised to keep the covenant too.

decisions.choice: by the pillar: the king's place in the temple court
decisions.reason: The king had a set place by a pillar at the temple, where Joash was shown to the people when he was crowned (11:14). Josiah stands there to make the covenant on behalf of the nation.

decisions.choice: made the covenant before Yahweh: Israel's covenant renewed
decisions.reason: "The covenant" is the bond already known between Yahweh and his people. Making it "before Yahweh" means in his presence, with him as the one to whom the promise is made. Jehoiada had renewed it in the same place after the years of Baal worship (11:17).

decisions.choice: commandments, testimonies and statutes: the whole of the covenant law
decisions.reason: The three words together name all that Yahweh requires (Deuteronomy 6:17). Commandments are what he orders; testimonies are the solemn terms of the covenant, declared before witnesses; statutes are laws laid down for good.

decisions.choice: with all the heart and with all the soul: the words of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy asks Israel to love and serve Yahweh "with all your heart and with all your soul" (Deuteronomy 6:5; 10:12; 30:2, 10). Verse 25 says that Josiah did so.

decisions.choice: all the people stood in the covenant: they took their stand on it
decisions.reason: To "stand in" the covenant is to take one's place in it and commit oneself to it. The same verb is used of the king standing by the pillar: king and people both take their stand.

decisions.choice: commandments, testimonies, statutes / commandments, decrees, statutes / commands, instructions, laws
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in these books. Balanced "with all his heart and all his being" and Readable "all his life" follow Deuteronomy 6:5, where "soul" means the whole living self.

decisions.choice: He promised ... all the people promised
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that making a covenant and standing in it meant making a promise.

source.text: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת־חִלְקִיָּהוּ֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל וְאֶת־כֹּהֲנֵ֣י הַמִּשְׁנֶה֮ וְאֶת־שֹׁמְרֵ֣י הַסַּף֒ לְהוֹצִיא֙ מֵהֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֣ת כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֗ים הָֽעֲשׂוּיִם֙ לַבַּ֣עַל וְלָֽאֲשֵׁרָ֔ה וּלְכֹ֖ל צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַֽיִּשְׂרְפֵ֞ם מִח֤וּץ לִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ בְּשַׁדְמ֣וֹת קִדְר֔וֹן וְנָשָׂ֥א אֶת־עֲפָרָ֖ם בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded the king Hilkiah the priest the great and [the] priests of the second [rank] and [the] keepers of the threshold to bring out from [the] temple of Yahweh all the vessels made for Baal and for Asherah and for all [the] host of the heavens; and he burned them outside Jerusalem in [the] fields of Kidron, and carried their dust [to] Bethel.

en.L: And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest and the priests of the second [rank] and the keepers of the threshold to bring out from the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all the vessels made for Baal and for Asherah and for all the host of the heavens; and he burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron and carried their dust [to] Bethel.
en.B: The king ordered Hilkiah the high priest, the priests next in rank and the keepers of the threshold to bring out of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all the objects made for Baal, for Asherah and for all the host of heaven. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron Valley and carried their ashes to Bethel.
en.R: The king ordered Hilkiah the high priest, the priests who served under him, and the men who guarded the temple doors to take out of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple everything that had been made for worshiping Baal, the goddess Asherah, and the stars in the sky. He burned all of it outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron Valley. Then he carried the ashes to Bethel.

decisions.choice: keepers of the threshold: the guards of the temple entrances
decisions.reason: These were senior temple officers who guarded the doors and received gifts brought in (12:10; 22:4). Three of them were taken with the high priest when Jerusalem fell (25:18).

decisions.choice: Baal, Asherah and the host of heaven: the worship Manasseh brought in
decisions.reason: Manasseh had built altars for Baal, made an Asherah, and worshiped all the host of heaven, the sun, moon and stars, even in the courts of the temple (21:3-7). Asherah was a Canaanite goddess (1 Kings 15:13). The vessels were the bowls, stands and other things used in that worship.

decisions.choice: the fields of Kidron: the open ground of the valley east of the city
decisions.reason: The Kidron Valley runs along the east side of Jerusalem. King Asa had burned his mother's image of Asherah there (1 Kings 15:13), and Josiah uses it again in verses 6 and 12.

decisions.choice: carried their dust to Bethel: to defile the north's chief sanctuary
decisions.reason: Bethel was where Jeroboam set up his golden calf and his own altar (1 Kings 12:28-33). Bringing the ashes of idols there made that place unclean too, before Josiah tore its altar down (verse 15).

decisions.choice: the host of the heavens (Literal); the host of heaven (Balanced); the stars in the sky (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Host" means an army: the stars and other lights of the sky pictured as a great company. Readable says what was worshiped.

decisions.choice: the men who guarded the temple doors; the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title of the doorkeepers and says who Asherah was.

source.text: וְהִשְׁבִּ֣ית אֶת־הַכְּמָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽתְנוּ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיְקַטֵּ֤ר בַּבָּמוֹת֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וּמְסִבֵּ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֶת־הַֽמְקַטְּרִ֣ים לַבַּ֗עַל לַשֶּׁ֤מֶשׁ וְלַיָּרֵ֨חַ֙ וְלַמַּזָּל֔וֹת וּלְכֹ֖ל צְבָ֥א הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he put an end to the idolatrous priests whom had appointed [the] kings of Judah, and he burned incense on the high places in [the] cities of Judah and [the] surroundings of Jerusalem, and those burning incense to Baal, to the sun and to the moon and to the constellations and to all [the] host of the heavens.

en.L: And he put an end to the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed, and [who] burned incense at the high places in the cities of Judah and the surroundings of Jerusalem, and those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun and to the moon and to the constellations and to all the host of the heavens.
en.B: He did away with the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense at the high places in the towns of Judah and around Jerusalem, and with those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun and the moon, to the constellations and to all the host of heaven.
en.R: He got rid of the priests who served idols. The kings of Judah had appointed them to burn incense at the hilltop shrines in the towns of Judah and in the places around Jerusalem. He also got rid of the people who burned incense to Baal, to the sun and moon, to the groups of stars, and to all the stars in the sky.

decisions.choice: idolatrous priests: priests who served other gods or idols
decisions.reason: The word used here (kemarim) is not the usual word for priest. In the Old Testament it is used only of priests of idols and other gods: of the calf at Bethel (Hosea 10:5) and of the priests Zephaniah condemns in Josiah's own day (Zephaniah 1:4). It marks them as priests of false worship.

decisions.choice: and he burned incense: the work these priests did
alternatives: whom the kings of Judah had appointed and who burned incense
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is singular, "and he burned incense", though the priests are many. It is best taken as describing what they were appointed for: they burned incense at the high places. The ancient translations read a plural, "and they burned incense".

decisions.choice: put an end to: removed them from their office
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something stop. It says that Josiah ended their service, not that he killed them; the priests of the northern shrines are treated differently in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the constellations: groups of stars, perhaps the signs of the zodiac
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It names star groups that were worshiped, probably the twelve signs through which the sun was seen to pass in the year (compare Job 38:32).

decisions.choice: idolatrous priests (Literal, Balanced); priests who served idols (Readable)
decisions.reason: The English shows that these were not Yahweh's priests (m1). Readable also says "groups of stars" for constellations and "the stars in the sky" for the host of heaven, as in verse 4.

source.text: וַיֹּצֵ֣א אֶת־הָאֲשֵׁרָה֩ מִבֵּ֨ית יְהוָ֜ה מִח֤וּץ לִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אֶל־נַ֣חַל קִדְר֔וֹן וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף אֹתָ֛הּ בְּנַ֥חַל קִדְר֖וֹן וַיָּ֣דֶק לְעָפָ֑ר וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ֙ אֶת־עֲפָרָ֔הּ עַל־קֶ֖בֶר בְּנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought out the Asherah from [the] house of Yahweh outside Jerusalem to [the] valley of Kidron, and burned it in [the] valley of Kidron and ground [it] to dust, and threw its dust on [the] grave[s] of [the] sons of the people.

en.L: And he brought out the Asherah pole from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, outside Jerusalem, to the Wadi Kidron, and burned it in the Wadi Kidron and ground [it] to dust, and threw its dust on the graves of the sons of the people.
en.B: He took the Asherah pole out of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the Kidron Valley outside Jerusalem. He burned it there in the Kidron Valley, ground it to dust and threw the dust on the graves of the common people.
en.R: He took the pole used to worship Asherah out of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and carried it outside Jerusalem to the Kidron Valley. He burned it there and crushed it into dust. Then he threw the dust on the graves of the common people.

decisions.choice: the Asherah: the image Manasseh set up in the temple
decisions.reason: Manasseh had made an image of Asherah and set it up in the house of which Yahweh had said "I will put my name there" (21:7). Josiah removes it from the temple and destroys it completely.

decisions.choice: the graves of the common people: a public burial ground
decisions.reason: The common people were buried in a shared burial place in the Kidron Valley (Jeremiah 26:23). Throwing the idol's dust there treated it as something unclean, fit only for the place of the dead. 2 Chronicles 34:4 says the dust was scattered on the graves of those who had sacrificed to the idols.

decisions.choice: the sons of the people: ordinary people
decisions.reason: "Sons of the people" means the common people, as distinct from the king's household and the leading families.

decisions.choice: the pole used to worship Asherah
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books. Literal and Balanced say "Asherah pole" for the singular "the Asherah", as at 18:4.

source.text: וַיִּתֹּץ֙ אֶת־בָּתֵּ֣י הַקְּדֵשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הַנָּשִׁ֗ים אֹרְג֥וֹת שָׁ֛ם בָּתִּ֖ים לָאֲשֵׁרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he tore down [the] houses of the male cult prostitutes which [were] in [the] house of Yahweh, where the women [were] weaving there houses for Asherah.

en.L: And he tore down the houses of the male cult prostitutes that [were] in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, where the women were weaving houses for Asherah.
en.B: He tore down the quarters of the male shrine prostitutes in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, where the women wove coverings for Asherah.
en.R: He tore down the rooms in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple used by the men who served as prostitutes at the shrines. In those rooms the women wove coverings for the goddess Asherah.

decisions.choice: male cult prostitutes: men attached to the shrines, probably for sexual rites
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 14:24 and 15:12, the word means "consecrated ones", men set apart for a shrine. The law forbids them (Deuteronomy 23:18). They are usually taken to be men who served as prostitutes in the worship of other gods, though some think the word means shrine servants in a wider sense.

decisions.choice: houses for Asherah: woven hangings or coverings for the image
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for "houses". What the women wove was perhaps tent-like hangings that sheltered the image of Asherah, or clothing for the image itself; Jeremiah 10:9 speaks of idols dressed in blue and purple cloth. The exact sense is not known.

decisions.choice: houses in the house of Yahweh: rooms or quarters in the temple courts
decisions.reason: The temple courts had side rooms and buildings (1 Kings 6:5; Jeremiah 35:4). Some of these had been given over to the worship of Asherah, even within the temple area.

decisions.choice: male cult prostitutes (Literal); male shrine prostitutes (Balanced); men who worked as prostitutes at the shrines (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording used for this word at 1 Kings 14:24.

decisions.choice: quarters, coverings (Balanced); rooms, coverings (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "houses" both times. Balanced and Readable say what the houses were in each place: rooms in the temple courts, and woven coverings for the image (m2, m3).

source.text: וַיָּבֵ֤א אֶת־כָּל־הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ מֵעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיְטַמֵּ֣א אֶת־הַבָּמ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִטְּרוּ־שָׁ֨מָּה֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים מִגֶּ֖בַע עַד־בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וְנָתַ֞ץ אֶת־בָּמ֣וֹת הַשְּׁעָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־פֶּ֜תַח שַׁ֤עַר יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ שַׂר־הָעִ֔יר אֲשֶֽׁר־עַל־שְׂמֹ֥אול אִ֖ישׁ בְּשַׁ֥עַר הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought all the priests from [the] cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where had burned incense there the priests, from Geba to Beersheba; and he broke down [the] high places of the gates which [were at the] entrance of [the] gate of Joshua [the] governor of the city, which [was] on [the] left of a man in [the] gate of the city.

en.L: And he brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba; and he broke down the high places of the gates that [were at the] entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which [was] on a man's left at the gate of the city.
en.B: He brought all the priests in from the towns of Judah and defiled the high places where those priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba. He broke down the high places of the gates that stood at the way into the Gate of Joshua, the city governor, on the left as one enters the city gate.
en.R: Josiah brought to Jerusalem all the priests from the towns of Judah. He made unclean the hilltop shrines where they had burned incense, from Geba in the north to Beersheba in the south. He also tore down the shrines at the gates. They stood at the entrance of the Gate of Joshua, the city governor, on the left as you went in through the city gate.

decisions.choice: he brought the priests in: worship gathered to one place
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 12 commands sacrifice only at the one place Yahweh chooses. Josiah brings the priests of the country shrines to Jerusalem and makes the shrines unusable, so that worship is gathered at the temple.

decisions.choice: from Geba to Beersheba: the whole of Judah, north to south
decisions.reason: Geba, in Benjamin, was on Judah's northern border (1 Kings 15:22); Beersheba was in the far south. The phrase means the whole land of Judah, as "from Dan to Beersheba" meant all Israel.

decisions.choice: defiled: made unfit for worship
decisions.reason: To defile a place of worship is to make it ritually unclean so that sacrifice can no longer be offered there. Verses 14, 16 and 20 show one way this was done, with human bones.

decisions.choice: the high places of the gates: shrines beside the city gates
alternatives: the high places of the goat-demons
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "the high places of the gates": shrines at the city gates. With a small change of letters the words would read "the high places of the goat-demons", the goat-idols forbidden in Leviticus 17:7. The Hebrew as it stands makes sense and is followed.

decisions.choice: on a man's left: on the left of someone entering
decisions.reason: The directions are given from the point of view of a person going in through the city gate.

decisions.choice: to Jerusalem; in the north ... in the south
decisions.reason: Readable says where the priests were brought and what the two place names mark.

source.text: אַ֗ךְ לֹ֤א יַֽעֲלוּ֙ כֹּהֲנֵ֣י הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֶל־מִזְבַּ֥ח יְהוָ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֛י אִם־אָכְל֥וּ מַצּ֖וֹת בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Only not went up [the] priests of the high places to [the] altar of Yahweh in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread(s) among their brothers.

en.L: However, the priests of the high places did not go up to the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.
en.B: The priests of the high places did not serve at the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread with their fellow priests.
en.R: The priests from the hilltop shrines were not allowed to serve at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s altar in Jerusalem. But they ate the bread made without yeast along with the other priests.

decisions.choice: go up to the altar: serve at it as priests
decisions.reason: The altar stood high, and a priest "went up" to it to offer sacrifices (1 Kings 12:32-33). These priests were not allowed to do the work of priests at the temple.

decisions.choice: ate unleavened bread among their brothers: they shared the priests' food
decisions.reason: Priests lived on their share of the offerings, and the grain offering was eaten as unleavened bread by the priests (Leviticus 6:9-11). These priests were fed from the priests' portion, though they could not serve.

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 18:6-8: Levites from the towns serving at the chosen place
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy allows a Levite from any town of Israel who comes to the chosen place to serve there and eat an equal share. The priests of Judah's high places were given a share but not the service, since they had served at forbidden shrines.

decisions.choice: their brothers: their fellow priests
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means their kinsmen in the priesthood, the priests who served at the temple.

decisions.choice: were not allowed to serve
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that this was not their choice. The Hebrew says only that they "did not go up", but the contrast with Deuteronomy 18:6-8 (m3) shows that they were kept from serving.

source.text: וְטִמֵּ֣א אֶת־הַתֹּ֔פֶת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּגֵ֣י בֶן־הִנֹּ֑ם לְבִלְתִּ֗י לְהַעֲבִ֨יר אִ֜ישׁ אֶת־בְּנ֧וֹ וְאֶת־בִּתּ֛וֹ בָּאֵ֖שׁ לַמֹּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he defiled the Topheth which [is] in [the] valley of Ben-hinnom, so that not to make pass a man his son or his daughter in the fire to Molech.

en.L: And he defiled Topheth, which [is] in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, so that no one might make his son or his daughter pass through the fire to Molech.
en.B: He defiled Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, so that no one would ever again make a son or daughter pass through the fire for Molech.
en.R: He made Topheth unclean. It was in the Valley of Ben-hinnom. He did this so that no one could ever again burn their son or daughter in the fire as a sacrifice to Molech.

decisions.choice: Topheth: the place of burning in the valley
decisions.reason: Topheth was the place in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned in sacrifice (Jeremiah 7:31-32; 19:5-6; Isaiah 30:33). The name may mean "fireplace", perhaps given the vowels of the word for "shame".

decisions.choice: the Valley of Ben-hinnom: the reading given in the margin (qere)
alternatives: the valley of the sons of Hinnom
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text (ketiv) read "the valley of the sons of Hinnom"; the reading passed down for reading aloud (qere) is "the valley of Ben-hinnom", "the son of Hinnom", as in Joshua 15:8. The reading aloud is followed. Both name the valley south of Jerusalem whose name later gave the word Gehenna.

decisions.choice: make pass through the fire: burn a child as an offering
decisions.reason: The phrase names the rite of offering a child by fire, forbidden in Deuteronomy 18:10. Ahaz and Manasseh had done it (16:3; 21:6).

decisions.choice: Molech: the god to whom children were burned
decisions.reason: The law forbids giving children to Molech (Leviticus 18:21; 20:2-5). The name comes from the word for "king" (1 Kings 11:7).

decisions.choice: burn their son or daughter in the fire as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: Readable says what "pass through the fire" meant, as at 16:3.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁבֵּ֣ת אֶת־הַסּוּסִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתְנוּ֩ מַלְכֵ֨י יְהוּדָ֤ה לַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ מִבֹּ֣א בֵית־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־לִשְׁכַּת֙ נְתַן־מֶ֣לֶךְ הַסָּרִ֔יס אֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּפַּרְוָרִ֑ים וְאֶת־מַרְכְּב֥וֹת הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ שָׂרַ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he removed the horses which had given [the] kings of Judah to the sun, from [the] entering of [the] house of Yahweh, by [the] chamber of Nathan-melech the eunuch, which [was] in the precincts; and the chariots of the sun he burned with fire.

en.L: And he removed the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun, from the entrance of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, by the chamber of Nathan-melech the eunuch, which [was] in the precincts; and the chariots of the sun he burned with fire.
en.B: He removed the horses the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun from the entrance to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, by the room of Nathan-melech the official, which was in the precincts. And he burned up the chariots of the sun.
en.R: The kings of Judah had set apart horses for the worship of the sun. They were kept at the entrance to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, near the room of an official named Nathan-melech, in the area beside the courtyard. Josiah got rid of those horses, and he burned the chariots used in worshiping the sun.

decisions.choice: horses and chariots of the sun: objects of sun worship
decisions.reason: Among the peoples around Israel the sun was pictured as a god who drove a chariot across the sky. The kings of Judah had dedicated horses and chariots to it, perhaps for processions. Ezekiel saw men in the temple court bowing to the sun in the east (Ezekiel 8:16). The law forbids worship of the sun (Deuteronomy 4:19; 17:3).

decisions.choice: the precincts: a court or annex beside the temple, not exactly known
decisions.reason: The word (parwarim) is found only here. It seems to name an open area or colonnade at the edge of the temple courts; a similar word is used of a place on the west side of the temple in 1 Chronicles 26:18.

decisions.choice: eunuch: a court official
decisions.reason: The word can mean a eunuch, but it is also used as a title for a high official at court (1 Kings 22:9; 2 Kings 8:6). Which is meant here cannot be known.

decisions.choice: from the entrance: the horses stood at the way into the temple
decisions.reason: The horses were kept near the way into the temple, and Josiah removed them from there.

decisions.choice: eunuch (Literal); official (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books (m3).

decisions.choice: the kings' act told first, then Josiah's
decisions.reason: Readable first explains what the horses were, then says what Josiah did with them.

source.text: וְאֶֽת־הַֽמִּזְבְּח֡וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַגָּג֩ עֲלִיַּ֨ת אָחָ֜ז אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֣וּ׀מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה וְאֶת־הַֽמִּזְבְּחוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֣ה מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה בִּשְׁתֵּ֛י חַצְר֥וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה נָתַ֣ץ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיָּ֣רָץ מִשָּׁ֔ם וְהִשְׁלִ֥יךְ אֶת־עֲפָרָ֖ם אֶל־נַ֥חַל קִדְרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And the altars which [were] on the roof, [the] upper room of Ahaz, which had made [the] kings of Judah, and the altars which had made Manasseh in [the] two courts of [the] house of Yahweh, pulled down the king, and he crushed [them] from there and threw their dust into [the] valley of Kidron.

en.L: And the altars that [were] on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the king pulled down; and he broke [them] in pieces from there and threw their dust into the Wadi Kidron.
en.B: The king pulled down the altars that the kings of Judah had made on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, and the altars Manasseh had built in the two courts of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He broke them in pieces and removed them from there, and he threw their dust into the Kidron Valley.
en.R: The kings of Judah had built altars on the roof of King Ahaz's upstairs room. Manasseh had built altars in the two courtyards of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. King Josiah pulled all these altars down. He smashed them to pieces, took them away, and threw the dust into the Kidron Valley.

decisions.choice: altars on the roof: for worship of the stars
decisions.reason: Flat roofs were used for offerings to the host of heaven, where the sky could be seen (Jeremiah 19:13; Zephaniah 1:5). The upper room of Ahaz was a room built on the palace roof; Ahaz had brought in other foreign forms of worship too (16:10-18).

decisions.choice: the altars Manasseh made in the two courts
decisions.reason: Manasseh had built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the temple (21:5).

decisions.choice: he broke them in pieces from there: a verb whose sense is not certain
alternatives: he hurried them away from there
decisions.reason: The verb can come from a root meaning "crush" or from one meaning "run". Read the first way, Josiah smashed the altars and removed them; read the second, he hurried them away from there.

decisions.choice: the altars named first: the weight falls on what was destroyed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the altars at the start of the sentence and the king and his act after them, as also in verses 13 and 15.

decisions.choice: the king named first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the subject first, as English does. Literal keeps the Hebrew order (m4).

source.text: וְֽאֶת־הַבָּמ֞וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀עַל־פְּנֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֮ מִימִ֣ין לְהַר־הַמַּשְׁחִית֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּ֠נָה שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לְעַשְׁתֹּ֣רֶת׀שִׁקֻּ֣ץ צִידֹנִ֗ים וְלִכְמוֹשׁ֙ שִׁקֻּ֣ץ מוֹאָ֔ב וּלְמִלְכֹּ֖ם תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־עַמּ֑וֹן טִמֵּ֖א הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the high places which [were] on [the] face of Jerusalem, which [were] from [the] right of [the] mountain of the destruction, which had built Solomon king of Israel for Ashtoreth [the] detestable thing of [the] Sidonians, and for Chemosh [the] detestable thing of Moab, and for Milcom [the] abomination of [the] sons of Ammon, defiled the king.

en.L: And the high places that [were] east of Jerusalem, which [were] to the south of the Mount of Destruction, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the detestable thing of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the detestable thing of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the sons of Ammon, the king defiled.
en.B: The king defiled the high places east of Jerusalem, south of the Mount of Destruction, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the detestable goddess of the Sidonians, for Chemosh the detestable god of Moab, and for Milcom the detestable god of the Ammonites.
en.R: King Josiah also made unclean the hilltop shrines east of Jerusalem, on the south side of the Mount of Destruction. Long before, King Solomon of Israel had built them for Ashtoreth, the disgusting goddess of the people of Sidon, for Chemosh, the disgusting god of Moab, and for Milcom, the disgusting god of the Ammonites.

decisions.choice: the shrines Solomon built: 1 Kings 11:5-7
decisions.reason: Solomon had built high places for the gods of his foreign wives on the hill east of Jerusalem (1 Kings 11:5-7), more than three hundred years before. 1 Kings 11:7 names the Ammonite god there as Molech, while 1 Kings 11:5 and 33 name him Milcom, as this verse does.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Destruction: a scornful name for the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: The hill east of Jerusalem is the Mount of Olives (1 Kings 11:7). "Mount of Destruction" is probably a play on a name like "Mount of Anointing", which sounds much the same in Hebrew, turned into a name that fits the shrines on it.

decisions.choice: detestable thing, abomination: scornful names for foreign gods
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 11:5, the writer does not call these gods "god" but uses words for something loathsome. The word used for Milcom here ("abomination") is the one used for practices Yahweh detests (1 Kings 14:24).

decisions.choice: on the face of Jerusalem, from the right: east of the city, to the south
decisions.reason: For someone facing the sunrise, the front is the east and the right hand is the south (1 Kings 11:7).

decisions.choice: detestable thing, abomination (Literal); detestable goddess, detestable god (Balanced); disgusting goddess, disgusting god (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of 1 Kings 11:5-7. Balanced and Readable use one word for both Hebrew terms; Literal keeps them apart (m3). "Goddess" for Ashtoreth as at 1 Kings 11:5.

decisions.choice: Long before
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader that Solomon had built these shrines long before Josiah's time (m1).

source.text: וְשִׁבַּר֙ אֶת־הַמַּצֵּב֔וֹת וַיִּכְרֹ֖ת אֶת־הָאֲשֵׁרִ֑ים וַיְמַלֵּ֥א אֶת־מְקוֹמָ֖ם עַצְמ֥וֹת אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he broke the standing stones and cut down the Asherah poles, and filled their place [with] bones of man.

en.L: And he broke the standing stones and cut down the Asherah poles, and filled their places [with] human bones.
en.B: He smashed the standing stones, cut down the Asherah poles, and filled the places where they had stood with human bones.
en.R: He smashed the stone pillars and cut down the poles used to worship Asherah. Then he covered the places where they had stood with human bones.

decisions.choice: broke the standing stones, cut down the Asherah poles: as Deuteronomy commands
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy tells Israel to break the standing stones of the nations and cut down or burn their Asherah poles (Deuteronomy 7:5; 12:3). Hezekiah had done the same (18:4).

decisions.choice: human bones: to make the places unclean
decisions.reason: Contact with a dead body or a human bone made a person or place unclean (Numbers 19:16). Bones left there made the sites unfit for worship ever again.

decisions.choice: stone pillars, poles used to worship Asherah
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in these books.

source.text: וְגַ֨ם אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֜חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֗ל הַבָּמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה יָרָבְעָ֤ם בֶּן־נְבָט֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱטִ֣יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל גַּ֣ם אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֧חַ הַה֛וּא וְאֶת־הַבָּמָ֖ה נָתָ֑ץ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֧ף אֶת־הַבָּמָ֛ה הֵדַ֥ק לְעָפָ֖ר וְשָׂרַ֥ף אֲשֵׁרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And also the altar which [was] at Bethel, the high place which had made Jeroboam son of Nebat who caused Israel to sin, also that altar and the high place he tore down; and he burned the high place, crushed [it] to dust, and burned [the] Asherah.

en.L: And also the altar that [was] at Bethel, the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, had made, even that altar and the high place he tore down; and he burned the high place, crushed [it] to dust, and burned the Asherah pole.
en.B: Even the altar at Bethel, the high place made by Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel to sin, even that altar and high place he tore down. He burned the high place and crushed it to dust, and he burned the Asherah pole.
en.R: Josiah also tore down the altar and the hilltop shrine at Bethel. Jeroboam son of Nebat had made them, and he had led Israel into sin. Josiah burned the shrine and crushed it to dust. He also burned the pole used to worship Asherah.

decisions.choice: the altar at Bethel that Jeroboam made: 1 Kings 12:28-33
decisions.reason: Jeroboam, the first king of the northern kingdom, set up a golden calf at Bethel and built an altar and a high place there, so that his people would not go to Jerusalem (1 Kings 12:28-33). Kings calls him the one "who caused Israel to sin" (1 Kings 14:16; 15:30), and judges every northern king by his sin.

decisions.choice: Bethel: in the old northern kingdom, now under Assyria
decisions.reason: Bethel lay just north of Judah's border, in the territory of the northern kingdom that Assyria had taken a century before (17:6, 24). As Assyria's power faded, Josiah was able to act there.

decisions.choice: he burned the high place: the shrine building and its wooden parts
decisions.reason: A high place could have a building and wooden objects that would burn. Josiah burned it, crushed what was left, and burned the Asherah pole that stood there.

decisions.choice: Even the altar ... even that altar
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the altar, breaks off to say whose it was, and then takes it up again: "also ... also that altar". Balanced keeps the repeated "even"; Readable puts it in one short sentence.

source.text: וַיִּ֣פֶן יֹאשִׁיָּ֗הוּ וַיַּ֨רְא אֶת־הַקְּבָרִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־שָׁם֙ בָּהָ֔ר וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־הָֽעֲצָמוֹת֙ מִן־הַקְּבָרִ֔ים וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וַֽיְטַמְּאֵ֑הוּ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרָא֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָרָ֔א אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And turned Josiah and saw the graves which [were] there on the mountain, and he sent and took the bones from the graves and burned [them] on the altar and defiled it, according to [the] word of Yahweh which called out [the] man of God who called out these things.

en.L: And Josiah turned and saw the tombs that [were] there on the mountain, and he sent and took the bones from the tombs and burned [them] on the altar and defiled it, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that the man of God called out, who had called out these things.
en.B: As Josiah turned around, he saw the tombs there on the hillside, and he sent men to take the bones out of the tombs. He burned them on the altar and so defiled it, in keeping with the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that the man of God had cried out when he foretold these things.
en.R: Then Josiah looked around and saw the tombs on the hillside. He sent men to take the bones out of them, and he burned the bones on the altar to make it unclean. This was just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen. The man of God had announced it long before, when he shouted these things at the altar.

decisions.choice: the word the man of God called out: 1 Kings 13:2
decisions.reason: When Jeroboam stood at this altar, a man of God from Judah cried out against it: a son of David's house named Josiah would sacrifice the priests of the high places on it, and human bones would be burned on it (1 Kings 13:2). Some three hundred years later, the word comes true to the letter.

decisions.choice: burning bones on the altar: making it unclean
decisions.reason: A dead body made unclean whatever it touched (Numbers 19:11-16). Burning human bones on the altar defiled it so that it could never be used again (1 Kings 13:2).

decisions.choice: the ancient Greek adds a longer text here
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation adds that this happened "when Jeroboam stood by the altar at the feast", and then: "And he turned and lifted his eyes to the tomb of the man of God who had called out these things." The extra words may have dropped out of the Hebrew because two lines ended alike, or they may have been added to make the story flow into verse 17. The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: called out (Literal); cried out (Balanced); shouted (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the man of God at 1 Kings 13:2, and each level keeps the word it used there, so that the reader can hear the prophecy and its fulfilment together.

decisions.choice: long before, when he shouted these things at the altar
decisions.reason: Readable says when and where the man of God gave his message, from 1 Kings 13:1-2.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֚ה הַצִּיּ֣וּן הַלָּ֔ז אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֣י רֹאֶ֑ה וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו אַנְשֵׁ֣י הָעִ֗יר הַקֶּ֤בֶר אִישׁ־הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣א מִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתָ עַ֖ל הַמִּזְבַּ֥ח בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, What [is] the monument the this which I see? And said to him the men of the city, The grave of the man of God who came from Judah and called out these things which you have done against the altar of Bethel.

en.L: And he said, "What [is] this monument that I see?" And the men of the city said to him, "[It is] the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and called out these things that you have done against the altar of Bethel."
en.B: He asked, "What is that grave marker I see?" The men of the town answered, "The man of God who came from Judah is buried there. He cried out against the altar of Bethel the very things you have done."
en.R: Josiah asked, "What is that grave marker I see over there?" The men of the town told him, "The man of God who came from Judah is buried there. He announced that you would do these very things to the altar at Bethel."

decisions.choice: monument: a marker set up over a grave
decisions.reason: The word means a stone or post marking a place, here a grave (Ezekiel 39:15).

decisions.choice: the man of God who came from Judah: 1 Kings 13
decisions.reason: The story of 1 Kings 13 began, "A man of God came from Judah to Bethel" (1 Kings 13:1). The old prophet of Bethel buried him in his own tomb (1 Kings 13:29-30). The townspeople still knew whose grave it was.

decisions.choice: these things that you have done: the prophecy and its fulfilment named together
decisions.reason: The men of the city say that the man of God called out the very things Josiah has just done. What was foretold and what was done are the same.

decisions.choice: called out / cried out / announced
decisions.reason: As in verse 16. Readable says "announced" here, since the man of God is not shouting at Josiah but foretelling what he would do.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַנִּ֣יחוּ ל֔וֹ אִ֖ישׁ אַל־יָנַ֣ע עַצְמֹתָ֑יו וַֽיְמַלְּטוּ֙ עַצְמֹתָ֔יו אֵ֚ת עַצְמ֣וֹת הַנָּבִ֔יא אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖א מִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Leave him alone; let no one disturb his bones. And they let escape his bones, with [the] bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.

en.L: And he said, "Let him rest; let no one disturb his bones." So they let his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.
en.B: "Leave him in peace," he said. "Let no one disturb his bones." So they spared his bones, together with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
en.R: "Leave him alone," Josiah said. "Do not let anyone move his bones." So they did not touch his bones or the bones of the old prophet who had come from Samaria.

decisions.choice: his bones with the prophet's bones: 1 Kings 13:31-32
decisions.reason: The old prophet of Bethel told his sons to bury him beside the man of God: "lay my bones beside his bones", for his word against the altar of Bethel would surely come true (1 Kings 13:31-32). Because the two lay together, the old prophet's bones were spared too.

decisions.choice: the prophet who came from Samaria: the old prophet of Bethel
decisions.reason: The old prophet lived in Bethel (1 Kings 13:11). Samaria here names the whole northern region, as in 1 Kings 13:32 and verse 19; he is the prophet of the north, set beside the man of God from Judah.

decisions.choice: let escape: spared
decisions.reason: The verb means to let something escape or slip away. The bones escaped the burning that came on the others.

decisions.choice: the old prophet
decisions.reason: Readable says which prophet is meant, as 1 Kings 13:11 calls him.

source.text: וְגַם֩ אֶת־כָּל־בָּתֵּ֨י הַבָּמ֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֜וּ מַלְכֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְהַכְעִ֔יס הֵסִ֖יר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לָהֶ֔ם כְּכָל־הַֽמַּעֲשִׂ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה בְּבֵֽית־אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And also all [the] houses of the high places which [were] in [the] cities of Samaria, which had made [the] kings of Israel to provoke to anger, removed Josiah; and he did to them according to all the deeds which he had done at Bethel.

en.L: And also all the houses of the high places that [were] in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke [{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}] to anger, Josiah removed; and he did to them according to all the deeds that he had done at Bethel.
en.B: Josiah also removed every shrine on the high places in the towns of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made, provoking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to anger. He did to them just what he had done at Bethel.
en.R: Josiah also got rid of all the hilltop shrines in the towns of Samaria. The kings of Israel had built them, and they had made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} angry by doing it. Josiah did to these shrines everything he had done at Bethel.

decisions.choice: the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria: 1 Kings 13:32
decisions.reason: The old prophet of Bethel had said that the word of the man of God would come true "against the altar in Bethel and against all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria" (1 Kings 13:32). Josiah now carries it out across the north.

decisions.choice: to provoke to anger: the Hebrew names no one
decisions.reason: The verb has no object in the Hebrew text, but Kings uses it again and again of provoking Yahweh (21:6; 1 Kings 16:33). The ancient Greek translation supplies the Lord as the one provoked.

decisions.choice: Samaria: the old northern kingdom, now an Assyrian province
decisions.reason: Samaria was the capital of the northern kingdom, and the name came to be used for the whole region, which Assyria had taken and resettled (17:24).

decisions.choice: the LORD
decisions.reason: Every level supplies the one who was provoked (m2). Literal puts it in brackets. Balanced follows the wording of 1 Kings 13:32: "every shrine on the high places in the towns of Samaria".

source.text: וַ֠יִּזְבַּח אֶת־כָּל־כֹּהֲנֵ֨י הַבָּמ֤וֹת אֲשֶׁר־שָׁם֙ עַל־הַֽמִּזְבְּח֔וֹת וַיִּשְׂרֹ֛ף אֶת־עַצְמ֥וֹת אָדָ֖ם עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּ֖שָׁב יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sacrificed all [the] priests of the high places who [were] there on the altars, and burned bones of man on them; and he returned [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: And he sacrificed all the priests of the high places who [were] there on the altars, and burned human bones on them; and he returned [to] Jerusalem.
en.B: He sacrificed all the priests of the high places who were there on the altars, and he burned human bones on them. Then he went back to Jerusalem.
en.R: He killed all the priests of the hilltop shrines there and offered them on their altars as sacrifices. He also burned human bones on the altars. Then he went back to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: sacrificed the priests and burned human bones: 1 Kings 13:2 fulfilled
decisions.reason: The man of God had said to the altar at Bethel: "he will sacrifice on you the priests of the high places ... and human bones will be burned on you" (1 Kings 13:2). Josiah does this to the altars of the north.

decisions.choice: sacrificed: killed as an offering is killed
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for slaughtering an animal in sacrifice. These priests of the northern shrines were put to death on their own altars, unlike the priests of Judah's high places, who were brought to Jerusalem and kept alive (verses 8-9).

decisions.choice: there: in the towns of Samaria
decisions.reason: "There" points back to the shrines of verse 19.

decisions.choice: killed ... and offered them on their altars as sacrifices
decisions.reason: Readable says what "sacrificed the priests" means, as it does at 1 Kings 13:2.

source.text: וַיְצַ֤ו הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר עֲשׂ֣וּ פֶ֔סַח לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֑ם כַּכָּת֕וּב עַ֛ל סֵ֥פֶר הַבְּרִ֖ית הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded the king all the people, saying, Make [a] Passover to Yahweh your God, as [it is] written on [the] book of the covenant the this.

en.L: And the king commanded all the people, saying, "Keep a Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, as [it is] written in this book of the covenant."
en.B: The king commanded all the people, "Keep the Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in the way that is written in this book of the covenant."
en.R: The king gave an order to all the people: "Celebrate the Passover to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, as this book of the covenant says."

decisions.choice: the Passover as written in the book: Deuteronomy 16:1-8
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy commands that the Passover be kept not in each town but "at the place that Yahweh your God will choose to make his name dwell" (Deuteronomy 16:2, 5-6). The first Passover was kept by families in their homes (Exodus 12). Josiah's Passover is kept by the whole nation together in Jerusalem (verse 23).

decisions.choice: make a Passover: keep the Passover
decisions.reason: To "make" or "do" the Passover is to keep the feast with its sacrifice and meal (Joshua 5:10).

decisions.choice: the fuller account in 2 Chronicles 35
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 35:1-19 tells of this Passover at length: the Levites, the lambs given by the king and his officials, and the singers.

decisions.choice: Keep (Literal, Balanced); Celebrate ... to honor (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "celebrate", the plainer word for keeping a feast, as at Joshua 5:10.

source.text: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א נַֽעֲשָׂה֙ כַּפֶּ֣סַח הַזֶּ֔ה מִימֵי֙ הַשֹּׁ֣פְטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁפְט֖וּ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכֹ֗ל יְמֵ֛י מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For not had been kept like the Passover the this from [the] days of the judges who judged Israel, and all [the] days of [the] kings of Israel and [the] kings of Judah.

en.L: For no [Passover] like this Passover had been kept from the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor [in] all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
en.B: No Passover like this had been kept since the time of the judges who judged Israel, nor through all the time of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
en.R: No Passover like this one had been celebrated since the days when judges led Israel, or during all the years when kings ruled Israel and Judah.

decisions.choice: like this Passover: in the way it was kept now
decisions.reason: The point is not that no Passover had been kept at all, but that none had been kept like this one: by the whole nation at the one place of worship, exactly as the book commanded. Hezekiah had kept a great Passover too, but some came to it unclean and it was held in the second month (2 Chronicles 30:2, 18).

decisions.choice: the judges who judged Israel: the leaders before the kings
decisions.reason: The judges were the leaders Yahweh raised up to rescue and govern Israel before there were kings (Judges 2:16). The phrase reaches back to the time after Joshua.

decisions.choice: 2 Chronicles 35:18: "since the days of Samuel the prophet"
decisions.reason: Chronicles says the same in other words: no Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel, the last of the judges.

decisions.choice: the judges who judged Israel (Literal, Balanced); judges led Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words since Judges. Literal supplies "Passover" in brackets, since the Hebrew leaves it to be understood.

source.text: כִּ֗י אִם־בִּשְׁמֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ נַעֲשָׂ֞ה הַפֶּ֧סַח הַזֶּ֛ה לַיהוָ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: But in [the] eighteenth year of the king Josiah was kept the Passover the this to Yahweh in Jerusalem.

en.L: But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover was kept to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem.
en.B: But this Passover was kept to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem in the eighteenth year of King Josiah.
en.R: But in the eighteenth year that Josiah was king, this Passover was celebrated in Jerusalem to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the eighteenth year of Josiah: the year the book was found
decisions.reason: The book was found in the eighteenth year of Josiah (22:3), about 622 BC. The reform, the covenant and the Passover all came in the same year.

decisions.choice: but: in contrast with all the years before
decisions.reason: The words set this Passover against the long time of verse 22 when none like it had been kept.

decisions.choice: celebrated ... to honor
decisions.reason: As in verse 21.

source.text: וְגַ֣ם אֶת־הָאֹב֣וֹת וְאֶת־הַ֠יִּדְּעֹנִים וְאֶת־הַתְּרָפִ֨ים וְאֶת־הַגִּלֻּלִ֜ים וְאֵ֣ת כָּל־הַשִּׁקֻּצִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִרְאוּ֙ בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בִּעֵ֖ר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ לְ֠מַעַן הָקִ֞ים אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֤י הַתּוֹרָה֙ הַכְּתֻבִ֣ים עַל־הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָצָ֛א חִלְקִיָּ֥הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And also the mediums and the spiritists and the household gods and the idols and all the detestable things which were seen in [the] land of Judah and in Jerusalem, burned away Josiah, in order to establish [the] words of the law written on the book which found Hilkiah the priest [in the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And also the mediums and the spiritists and the household gods and the idols and all the detestable things that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, Josiah purged, in order to carry out the words of the law that were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found [in the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Josiah also purged the mediums and the spiritists, the household gods, the idols and all the detestable things to be seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem. He did this so as to carry out the words of the law, as they were written in the book Hilkiah the priest had discovered in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Josiah also got rid of the people who said they could talk with the dead or with spirits. He got rid of the household idols, the other idols, and all the disgusting things people worshiped in Judah and Jerusalem. Josiah did this to obey the teaching written in the book that the priest Hilkiah had found in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

decisions.choice: mediums and spiritists: those who claimed to speak with the dead and with spirits
decisions.reason: The law forbids consulting them (Leviticus 19:31; Deuteronomy 18:11), and Manasseh had appointed them (21:6). The words may name the practitioners or the spirits and objects they used; either way, their practice is what Josiah ended.

decisions.choice: household gods: teraphim, images used in the home and for seeking omens
decisions.reason: Teraphim were small images kept in a household (Genesis 31:19) and sometimes used to ask for guidance (Ezekiel 21:26).

decisions.choice: idols, detestable things: scornful words for images of other gods
decisions.reason: The word for idols is used only with contempt and may come from a word for dung (1 Kings 15:12). "Detestable things" is the word used for Milcom in 1 Kings 11:5.

decisions.choice: purged: burned away, removed completely
decisions.reason: The verb means to burn, and so to clear away completely. It is used in Deuteronomy's command "you shall purge the evil from among you" (Deuteronomy 13:6; 17:7).

decisions.choice: the law: the instruction written in the book
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy, the word (torah) means instruction, the whole of what the book teaches, and not only rules (Deuteronomy 1:5).

decisions.choice: mediums, spiritists (Literal, Balanced); people who said they could talk with the dead or with spirits (Readable); household gods / household idols
decisions.reason: The wording used at 1 Samuel 28:3, and the wording kept for teraphim in these books. Readable says "teaching" for the law, as in Deuteronomy.

source.text: וְכָמֹהוּ֩ לֹֽא־הָיָ֨ה לְפָנָ֜יו מֶ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֤ב אֶל־יְהוָה֙ בְּכָל־לְבָב֤וֹ וּבְכָל־נַפְשׁוֹ֙ וּבְכָל־מְאֹד֔וֹ כְּכֹ֖ל תּוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֑ה וְאַחֲרָ֖יו לֹֽא־קָ֥ם כָּמֹֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And like him not was before him [a] king who turned to Yahweh with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his might, according to all [the] law of Moses; and after him not arose like him.

en.L: And before him there was no king like him, who turned to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his power, according to all the law of Moses; and after him none like him arose.
en.B: Before him there was no king like him, who turned to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with his whole heart, with his whole being, and with all his strength, in keeping with all the law of Moses; and after him no one like him arose.
en.R: There had never been a king like Josiah. He turned to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all his heart, with all his life, and with all his strength. He obeyed all the teaching of Moses. And no king like him ever came after him.

decisions.choice: with all his heart, soul and might: Deuteronomy 6:5
decisions.reason: These are the words of the command "you shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength" (Deuteronomy 6:5). This is the only other place where the three are found together. Josiah is the king who did what the law asks above everything.

decisions.choice: turned: returned to Yahweh
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn or return, and is used for turning back to Yahweh in repentance (Deuteronomy 30:2, 10; 1 Kings 8:48). Verse 26 uses the same verb: Josiah turned to Yahweh, but Yahweh did not turn from his anger.

decisions.choice: might, strength: everything one has and can do
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 6:5, the word that usually means "very" is used as a noun for all one's power and means.

decisions.choice: none like him before or after: the highest praise
decisions.reason: Hezekiah too is praised as having no equal among the kings of Judah, for his trust in Yahweh (18:5). Josiah is praised for turning to Yahweh and keeping the whole law of Moses.

decisions.choice: with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his power / with his whole heart, with his whole being, and with all his strength / with all his heart, with all his life, and with all his strength
decisions.reason: Each level uses its own wording of Deuteronomy 6:5, so that the reader can hear the command behind the praise (m1).

decisions.choice: There had never been a king like Josiah
decisions.reason: Readable names the king and says first that he had no equal, then what he did. It says "teaching" for the law, as in Deuteronomy.

source.text: אַ֣ךְ׀לֹֽא־שָׁ֣ב יְהוָ֗ה מֵחֲר֤וֹן אַפּוֹ֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל אֲשֶׁר־חָרָ֥ה אַפּ֖וֹ בִּֽיהוּדָ֑ה עַ֚ל כָּל־הַכְּעָסִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִכְעִיס֖וֹ מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: Only not turned Yahweh from [the] burning of his anger the great, which burned his anger against Judah, because of all the provocations with which provoked him Manasseh.

en.L: Yet {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not turn from the burning of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great anger, with which {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger burned against Judah because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Even so, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not turn away from the fierceness of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great anger, which burned against Judah because of all the ways Manasseh had provoked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Even so, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not turn away from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great anger against Judah. It still burned because of all that Manasseh had done to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry.

decisions.choice: did not turn: the same verb as in verse 25
decisions.reason: Josiah "turned" to Yahweh with all his heart (verse 25), but Yahweh did not "turn" from his anger. The repeated verb sets the king's turning against the judgment that still stands.

decisions.choice: the provocations of Manasseh: 21:10-15
decisions.reason: Manasseh's sins had brought Yahweh's word that he would wipe Jerusalem as one wipes a dish (21:10-15). Huldah had told Josiah that the disaster would still come, though not in his days (22:16-20).

decisions.choice: the anger stands: one king's faithfulness does not undo the nation's long sin
decisions.reason: Kings does not say that Josiah's reform was in vain. It says that the judgment on Judah, earned over many reigns, was not taken back.

decisions.choice: the fierceness of his great anger
decisions.reason: The word means the burning or heat of anger. Balanced says "fierceness"; Literal keeps "burning".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה גַּ֤ם אֶת־יְהוּדָה֙ אָסִיר֙ מֵעַ֣ל פָּנַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲסִרֹ֖תִי אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּ֠מָאַסְתִּי אֶת־הָעִ֨יר הַזֹּ֤את אֲשֶׁר־בָּחַ֨רְתִּי֙ אֶת־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְאֶת־הַבַּ֔יִת אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְתִּי יִהְיֶ֥ה שְׁמִ֖י שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh, Also Judah I will remove from upon my face, as I removed Israel, and I will reject the city the this which I chose, Jerusalem, and the house which I said, My name will be there.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Judah too I will remove from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight, as I removed Israel, and I will reject this city that I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name will be there.'"
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I will remove Judah from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight too, as I removed Israel. I will reject this city I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name will be there.'"
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I will send the people of Judah away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, just as I sent Israel away. I will reject Jerusalem, the city I chose, and the temple where I said {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name would be."

decisions.choice: remove Judah as I removed Israel: 17:18-23
decisions.reason: Yahweh had removed Israel from his sight and sent it into exile in Assyria (17:18, 23). Judah will go the same way (21:13).

decisions.choice: my name will be there: the temple as the place Yahweh claimed as his own
decisions.reason: Yahweh's name stands for his presence and his claim of ownership. He had said that his name would be in the temple (1 Kings 8:29; 9:3; Deuteronomy 12:5). Even the chosen city and its temple will not be spared.

decisions.choice: Yahweh said: his word through the prophets
decisions.reason: The verse does not say when or to whom Yahweh said this. It sums up his word spoken through the prophets in Manasseh's time (21:10-15).

decisions.choice: send the people of Judah away from me; the temple
decisions.reason: Readable says what "remove from my sight" meant: exile. "The house" is the temple.

source.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Josiah and all that he did, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Judah?

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Josiah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
en.B: The rest of the acts of Josiah, and all that he did, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.
en.R: Everything else Josiah did is written in the history of the kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah: a royal record the writer could consult
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Kings (12:20; 1 Kings 15:7), the writer sends the reader to a fuller written record of Judah's kings, now lost. The question "are they not written ...?" means "they are written".

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: As in the sources formula throughout these books, Balanced and Readable state as a fact what the Hebrew asks as a question; Literal keeps the question.

source.text: בְּיָמָ֡יו עָלָה֩ פַרְעֹ֨ה נְכֹ֧ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֛יִם עַל־מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר עַל־נְהַר־פְּרָ֑ת וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ֙ לִקְרָאת֔וֹ וַיְמִיתֵ֨הוּ֙ בִּמְגִדּ֔וֹ כִּרְאֹת֖וֹ אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: In his days went up Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt to [the] king of Assyria to [the] river Euphrates; and went the king Josiah to meet him, and he killed him at Megiddo when he saw him.

en.L: In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria, to the river Euphrates. And King Josiah went to meet him, and [Neco] killed him at Megiddo when he saw him.
en.B: In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River, and King Josiah marched out to meet him. When Neco saw him, he killed him at Megiddo.
en.R: While Josiah was king, Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt marched north to the Euphrates River to help the king of Assyria. King Josiah went out to face Neco. But as soon as Neco saw him at Megiddo, he killed him.

decisions.choice: to the king of Assyria: to help him
decisions.reason: The word can mean "to" or "against". Records from the time show that in 609 BC Egypt marched north to support what was left of Assyria against the rising power of Babylon, so Neco went up to join the king of Assyria, not to fight him.

decisions.choice: went to meet him: went out to confront him
decisions.reason: To go "to meet" a king on the march can mean to go out against him. 2 Chronicles 35:20-24 tells of a battle in which Josiah was wounded by archers and died after being taken back to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: when he saw him: at their first meeting
decisions.reason: The words stress how quickly it ended: as soon as Neco met Josiah, he killed him.

decisions.choice: Megiddo: a fortress guarding the main pass into the Jezreel Valley
decisions.reason: Megiddo controlled the road from the coast to the north, the way an army from Egypt had to take to reach Syria and the Euphrates.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh Neco: Neco II, king of Egypt
decisions.reason: "Pharaoh" is the Egyptian king's title, and Neco his name. He ruled Egypt from about 610 to 595 BC.

decisions.choice: marched north ... to help the king of Assyria; to face Neco
decisions.reason: Readable follows m1 and m2, saying why Neco marched and what Josiah went out to do.

source.text: וַיַּרְכִּבֻ֨הוּ עֲבָדָ֥יו מֵת֙ מִמְּגִדּ֔וֹ וַיְבִאֻ֨הוּ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֖הוּ בִּקְבֻֽרָת֑וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח עַם־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת־יְהֽוֹאָחָז֙ בֶּן־יֹ֣אשִׁיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּמְשְׁח֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֹת֖וֹ תַּ֥חַת אָבִֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And made him ride his servants dead from Megiddo, and brought him [to] Jerusalem and buried him in his grave; and took [the] people of the land Jehoahaz son of Josiah, and anointed him and made him king in place of his father.

en.L: And his servants carried him dead [in a chariot] from Megiddo and brought him [to] Jerusalem and buried him in his own tomb. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and anointed him and made him king in place of his father.
en.B: His officials carried his body in a chariot from Megiddo and brought him to Jerusalem, where they buried him in his own tomb. The people of the land then took Jehoahaz son of Josiah; they anointed him and made him king in place of his father.
en.R: His officials put his body in a chariot and brought it from Megiddo to Jerusalem. They buried him in the tomb that was his own. After that, the people of the land chose Josiah's son Jehoahaz. They anointed him and made him king in his father's place.

decisions.choice: made him ride: carried him in a chariot
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone ride, here in a chariot. 2 Chronicles 35:24 says his servants took him out of his chariot and put him in his second chariot.

decisions.choice: his servants: the king's officials
decisions.reason: The king's servants are the men of his court and army.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the citizens of Judah
decisions.reason: As in 11:14 and 21:24, the free people of Judah as a body act to put a king on the throne. They chose Jehoahaz over his older brother Eliakim (verses 31, 36).

decisions.choice: anointed him: made him king with oil
decisions.reason: Pouring oil on the head set a man apart as king (1 Kings 1:39; 2 Kings 11:12).

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the king's servants in these books.

source.text: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְשָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ יְהוֹאָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ חֲמוּטַ֥ל בַּֽת־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִלִּבְנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] son of twenty and three year[s] [was] Jehoahaz when he became king, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

en.L: A son of twenty-three years [was] Jehoahaz when he became king, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother [was] Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
en.B: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
en.R: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for three months. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

decisions.choice: Jehoahaz: also called Shallum
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 22:11 and 1 Chronicles 3:15 call this son of Josiah Shallum. Jehoahaz, "Yahweh has grasped", may have been the name he took as king. Kings uses Jehoahaz throughout.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah from Libnah: not the prophet
decisions.reason: This Jeremiah was from Libnah, a town in the lowland of Judah (8:22; 19:8). The prophet Jeremiah came from Anathoth (Jeremiah 1:1). Hamutal was also the mother of Zedekiah (24:18), so Jehoahaz and Zedekiah were full brothers.

decisions.choice: a son of twenty-three years: twenty-three years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being the son of so many years (12:1).

decisions.choice: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king
decisions.reason: The accession formula is worded as throughout these books. Readable splits it into short sentences.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֖וּ אֲבֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, according to all that had done his fathers.

en.L: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to all that his fathers had done.
en.B: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as his ancestors had done.
en.R: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, just as his ancestors had done.

decisions.choice: did the evil in the eyes of Yahweh: the verdict on his reign
decisions.reason: Even in a reign of three months, Kings passes its verdict. After Josiah, each of the last four kings of Judah is judged in the same words (verse 37; 24:9, 19).

decisions.choice: his fathers: the kings before him
decisions.reason: "Fathers" means ancestors, here the kings of Judah who did evil, such as Manasseh and Amon (21:2, 20), not his father Josiah.

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil; ancestors
decisions.reason: The verdict formula is worded the same way at each level in these books. Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers".

source.text: וַיַּאַסְרֵהוּ֩ פַרְעֹ֨ה נְכֹ֤ה בְרִבְלָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֔ת מִמְּלֹ֖ךְבִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּתֶּן־עֹ֨נֶשׁ֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ מֵאָ֥ה כִכַּר־כֶּ֖סֶף וְכִכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And bound him Pharaoh Neco at Riblah in [the] land of Hamath, from reigning in Jerusalem; and he put a fine on the land, a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

en.L: And Pharaoh Neco put him in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that [he would] not reign in Jerusalem; and he imposed a fine on the land, 100 talents of silver and a talent of gold.
en.B: Pharaoh Neco put him in chains at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that he could no longer reign in Jerusalem, and he imposed on the land a payment of {{units:about 7,500 pounds|100 talents}} of silver and {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}} of gold.
en.R: Pharaoh Neco took Jehoahaz prisoner at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that he could no longer rule in Jerusalem. Neco forced the land of Judah to pay {{units:about 7,500 pounds|100 talents}} of silver and {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}} of gold.

decisions.choice: so that he would not reign: the reading given in the margin (qere)
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text (ketiv) read "when he reigned in Jerusalem"; the reading passed down for reading aloud (qere) is "from reigning", that is, to stop him reigning. The reading aloud is followed. 2 Chronicles 36:3 says that the king of Egypt removed him from the throne in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Riblah in the land of Hamath: Neco's base in Syria
decisions.reason: Riblah lay on the Orontes River in Syria, in the region of the city of Hamath. Neco made it his headquarters, as Nebuchadnezzar later did, and it was there that Zedekiah was judged (25:6, 20-21).

decisions.choice: a fine: a payment laid on a conquered land
decisions.reason: The word means a penalty or fine. Here it is the tribute Judah had to pay as a land now under Egypt's control.

decisions.choice: a talent: about 75 pounds of metal
decisions.reason: A talent was the largest weight, about 75 pounds. The sum was smaller than Hezekiah's payment to Assyria, 300 talents of silver and 30 of gold (18:14).

decisions.choice: about 7,500 pounds ... about 75 pounds
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give modern weights, with the talents as the alternative; Literal keeps the talents.

source.text: וַיַּמְלֵךְ֩ פַּרְעֹ֨ה נְכֹ֜ה אֶת־אֶלְיָקִ֣ים בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּ֗הוּ תַּ֚חַת יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֔יו וַיַּסֵּ֥ב אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוֹיָקִ֑ים וְאֶת־יְהוֹאָחָ֣ז לָקָ֔ח וַיָּבֹ֥א מִצְרַ֖יִם וַיָּ֥מָת שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And made king Pharaoh Neco Eliakim son of Josiah in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name [to] Jehoiakim; and Jehoahaz he took, and he came [to] Egypt and died there.

en.L: And Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name [to] Jehoiakim; and Jehoahaz he took away, and he came [to] Egypt and died there.
en.B: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in the place of Josiah his father. He changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim. Jehoahaz, though, he took away, and Jehoahaz went to Egypt and died there.
en.R: Pharaoh Neco made Josiah's son Eliakim king in place of his father Josiah. He changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim. Neco took Jehoahaz away to Egypt, and Jehoahaz died there.

decisions.choice: changed his name: a sign of Egypt's power over the king
decisions.reason: An overlord who gave a king a new name showed that the king ruled by his will. Nebuchadnezzar later did the same, changing Mattaniah's name to Zedekiah (24:17).

decisions.choice: Eliakim, Jehoiakim: "God raises up" and "Yahweh raises up"
decisions.reason: The two names mean almost the same. The new one replaces the general word for God with the name of Yahweh, the God of Judah. Neco did not give him the name of an Egyptian god.

decisions.choice: he came to Egypt and died there: Jehoahaz
decisions.reason: The subject of "came" and "died" is Jehoahaz. Jeremiah 22:10-12 says of Shallum, that is Jehoahaz, that he would never return but would die in the place where he was taken captive.

decisions.choice: in place of Josiah his father: as if Jehoahaz had not reigned
decisions.reason: Neco set Eliakim in Josiah's place, passing over the three months of Jehoahaz, whom the people of the land had chosen (verse 30).

decisions.choice: Jehoahaz went to Egypt and died there
