decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jehoahaz as the one who died, following m3. Literal keeps the Hebrew "he".

source.text: וְהַכֶּ֣סֶף וְהַזָּהָ֗ב נָתַ֤ן יְהוֹיָקִים֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה אַ֚ךְ הֶעֱרִ֣יךְ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ לָתֵ֥ת אֶת־הַכֶּ֖סֶף עַל־פִּ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה אִ֣ישׁ כְּעֶרְכּ֗וֹ נָגַ֞שׂ אֶת־הַכֶּ֤סֶף וְאֶת־הַזָּהָב֙ אֶת־עַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ לָתֵ֖ת לְפַרְעֹ֥ה נְכֹֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the silver and the gold gave Jehoiakim to Pharaoh; only he assessed the land to give the silver by [the] mouth of Pharaoh; each according to his assessment he exacted the silver and the gold from [the] people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Neco.

en.L: And the silver and the gold Jehoiakim gave to Pharaoh; but he assessed the land to give the silver at the command of Pharaoh; each according to his assessment, he exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Neco.
en.B: Jehoiakim paid Pharaoh the silver and the gold, but to raise the money Pharaoh demanded he had to tax the land. He exacted the silver and gold from the people of the land, each paying the amount assessed, to give to Pharaoh Neco.
en.R: Jehoiakim paid Pharaoh the silver and gold he demanded. To do this, he taxed the land. He made the people of the land pay silver and gold, each person according to what they owned, and he gave it to Pharaoh Neco.

decisions.choice: assessed: set a value on what each owned
decisions.reason: The verb means to set a value, as a priest set the value of a vow (Leviticus 27:8, 12). Jehoiakim had each man's wealth valued and taxed by it. Menahem of Israel had raised Assyria's tribute in a similar way (15:20).

decisions.choice: exacted: forced payment, as an oppressor
decisions.reason: The verb is used of taskmasters driving people to work (Exodus 5:6) and of creditors pressing for payment (Deuteronomy 15:2).

decisions.choice: by the mouth of Pharaoh: at Pharaoh's command
decisions.reason: The "mouth" of a ruler is his spoken order.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: those who had made Jehoahaz king
decisions.reason: The same people of the land who had chosen Jehoahaz (verse 30) now bore the cost of Egypt's rule.

decisions.choice: according to what they owned
decisions.reason: Readable says what the assessment was based on (m1).

source.text: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָ֨ה יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ זְבוּדָּ֥ה בַת־פְּדָיָ֖ה מִן־רוּמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] son of twenty and five year[s] [was] Jehoiakim when he became king, and eleven year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Zebudah daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.

en.L: A son of twenty-five years [was] Jehoiakim when he became king, and eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother [was] Zebudah daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.
en.B: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebudah daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.
en.R: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother was Zebudah, the daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.

decisions.choice: Zebudah: the reading given in the margin (qere)
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text (ketiv) give the name as Zebidah; the reading passed down for reading aloud (qere) is Zebudah. The reading aloud is followed.

decisions.choice: twenty-five years old: older than Jehoahaz
decisions.reason: Jehoiakim was two years older than Jehoahaz (verse 31), yet the people of the land had passed him over. His mother was a different wife of Josiah. His reign, about 609 to 598 BC, goes on into chapter 24.

decisions.choice: Rumah: a town not certainly known
decisions.reason: Rumah is not named elsewhere in the Old Testament. It may be a place in Galilee, which would mean Josiah married into a family from the old northern kingdom.

decisions.choice: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king
decisions.reason: As in verse 31.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֖וּ אֲבֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, according to all that had done his fathers.

en.L: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to all that his fathers had done.
en.B: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as his ancestors had done.
en.R: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil, just as his ancestors had done.

decisions.choice: did the evil in the eyes of Yahweh: the verdict on Jehoiakim
decisions.reason: The same verdict as on his brother (verse 32). Jeremiah tells of his reign: he burned the scroll of Jeremiah's prophecies (Jeremiah 36:23) and built his palace with unpaid labor (Jeremiah 22:13-19).

decisions.choice: the verdict formula; ancestors
decisions.reason: As in verse 32.
